subject: Notice: DataVault storage region change — SG roll-out & evidence
messages:
From: Anna Torres <anna.torres@datavaultinc.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: DataVault Security <security@datavaultinc.com>, Contracts <contracts@datavaultinc.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Notice: planned storage region roll-out to Singapore (SG) — details and Qs

Hi Sean,

Quick heads-up: DataVault will begin migrating a portion of our object storage for backups and indexing to our Singapore (ap-southeast-1) cluster on 2026-11-18. This change enables lower latency for APAC customers and is limited to encrypted at-rest backups and search indexes — primary customer data stores remain in existing regions unless otherwise agreed.

We wanted to surface the change early so Redwood can assess any cross-border/data transfer implications. High level:
- Scope: backup snapshots + index shards for customers with APAC presence.
- Timing: phased rollout starting 2026-11-18, estimated 3 weeks.
- Controls: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, customer keys can be BYOK via our KMS integration.

Attached: (1) SOC 2 Type II summary, (2) KMS topology diagram, (3) current subprocessor roster.

Please let us know:
1) Whether you need signed attestation of SCCs or alternate transfer mechanism for EU accounts;
2) If Redwood requires dataflow diagrams specific to our handling of Redwood customer backups;
3) Any evidence we should provide for your audit team (logs, key custody details, certificate rotation timeline).

Thanks,
Anna Torres
Head of Customer Security
DataVault Inc.
[Attachment: datavault-soc2-type2-2026.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: datavault-kms-topology-2026.png (PNG)]
[Attachment: datavault-subprocessor-roster-2026.csv (CSV)]

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna.torres@datavaultinc.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: planned storage region roll-out to Singapore (SG) — details and Qs

Anna — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments.

We’ll triage this with Security & Legal. Immediate asks from my side: please confirm whether the roster change introduces any new subprocessors that will have access to Redwood customer data in plain text (i.e., decryption capability) and whether key material will ever leave the KMS boundary you manage.

I’ll loop in Evelyn and Marcus to coordinate next steps for impacted accounts and any outreach to customers in EU.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna.torres@datavaultinc.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: planned storage region roll-out to Singapore (SG) — details and Qs

Hi Anna — Evelyn from Redwood Security.

Thanks for the documentation. A few clarifying requests we need to complete our compliance review:

1) Subprocessor access matrix: for each subprocessors listed in datavault-subprocessor-roster-2026.csv, indicate whether they have any of the following: (a) access to PII in plaintext, (b) access to encryption keys (KMS/HSM), (c) administrative access to storage clusters. A CSV with columns [subprocessor, role, plaintext_access, key_access, admin_access] would be ideal.

2) KMS details: does BYOK mean the customer-managed key origin is an HSM within DataVault’s control, or can Redwood supply a key stored in our KMS/HSM (i.e., external key import)? Please include the key wrapping and rotation process and whether key material ever transfers between regions.

3) Evidence: for EU customers we will need either (a) your signed SCC annexes or (b) a description of the legal basis for transfers + sample contract language.

4) Logs: can you provide a sample of the storage movement audit trail (obfuscated) showing object transfer events and IPs, and the retention policy for those logs?

If you can turn these around by EOD 2026-11-11 we can confirm impacted account communications and any required contract addenda.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------

From: DataVault Security <security@datavaultinc.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Torres <anna.torres@datavaultinc.com>, Contracts <contracts@datavaultinc.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 07:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: planned storage region roll-out to Singapore (SG) — details and Qs

Hi Evelyn / Sean,

Thanks for the detailed checklist — see answers below and attachments. Summary: no new subprocessors will receive plaintext decryption capability as part of this rollout. Key points: 

- Subprocessor matrix: attached CSV (datavault-subprocessor-roster-2026.csv) updated with boolean flags for plaintext_access, key_access, admin_access.
- KMS: BYOK supports two modes: (1) customer-imported key material (external KMS import) — DataVault will store wrapped key material inside a customer-dedicated HSM partition; (2) DataVault-managed KMS where keys never leave our HSMs. We do not export raw key material between regions. Rotation: quarterly with asymmetric wrapping; timeline in KMS diagram.
- SCCs / legal: we have an executed SCC addendum template; Contracts is available to sign and annotate. If you prefer, we can provide an explanatory memo referencing the transfer safeguards.
- Audit logs: attached a redacted transfer audit sample and retention schedule.

Attachments: datavault-subprocessor-roster-2026.csv (updated), datavault-kms-topology-2026.png (annotated), datavault-soc2-type2-2026.pdf (full report).

Let us know if you need notarized statements or a remote walkthrough of the key management controls.

—DataVault Security
[Attachment: datavault-subprocessor-roster-2026.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: datavault-kms-topology-2026.png (PNG)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: DataVault Security <security@datavaultinc.com>, Anna Torres <anna.torres@datavaultinc.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: planned storage region roll-out to Singapore (SG) — details and Qs

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the updated roster. Quick internal note: Evelyn — I’ll flag any EU-customer impacts in the SEC-341 ticket and route the SCC addendum to Contracts for signature. Marcus — please prepare a short customer advisory for accounts with APAC presence; suggest we include the high-level controls and an opt-out timeline.

Anna / DataVault — two small follow-ups before we close this out:
- Can Contracts send the SCC addendum draft into our shared DocuSign link (or hubspot attachment) so we can track execution?
- Can you confirm whether certificate rotation for the storage cluster will be completed before 2026-11-18 (we’d like the new certs in place prior to the first bulk movement).

If both items are confirmed, we’ll treat this as a notified subprocessor-region change with no additional mitigation required.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
